thread:
Sara: Heads-up — customer acme-api is getting a flood of invalid-JSON parse errors from JSON mode after a sudden billing spike. They say it started after a token rotation. Example paste below, anyone seen this cascade before?

Brian: Can you drop a request_id and a tiny snippet of the raw response?

Sara: request_id: req_0a1b2c, model: redwood-large, mode: json, sdk:js@2.4.1. Raw stream snippet they captured (truncated):
```
{"user": "acme", "items": [ {"id": 1}, {"id": 2}  // truncated...
<html>403 Forbidden</html>
```
So the stream has JSON then an HTML error appended, parse fails on client.

Cheng: That pattern screams HTTP error getting injected into the stream (expired/rotated token -> 403 HTML). If SDK starts parsing before status check we end up with mixed payload. Confirm SDK version — older clients did stream body before status check.

Anna: Also their retry loop is brutal — client retries every 100ms until parse succeeds, which multiplied requests and caused the billing spike. Recommend exponential backoff + jitter and a max retry cap. Example: initial=500ms, factor=2, max=8s, jitter +/-50%.

Brian: Triage checklist for support engineers: 1) confirm HTTP status and content-type before attempting JSON parse, 2) capture raw_response (base64 if long), 3) log sdk_version + request_id + client_ip, 4) check for 4xx/5xx injection. If 200+content-type!=application/json, treat as error.

Sara: Repro steps I sent to customer to confirm locally:
```bash
# expired token -> server returns HTML in stream
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer EXPIRED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"mode":"json","prompt":"..."}'
```
They see HTTP/1.1 403 and HTML body appended mid-stream.

Cheng: Fix guidance for SDKs: don't start JSON decode until status==200 and content-type header includes "application/json"; for streaming, buffer until the first chunk confirms headers. Also add a handler that if parse fails, check raw stream for non-printable or HTML tags.

Brian: Self-heal strategy we recommend to customers (use sparingly): if parse fails after verifying 200 and content-type, 1) try a lightweight cleanup to remove leading garbage then parse, 2) if still fails, re-ask model with a clarifying prompt asking to re-output only the JSON payload. Example re-ask prompt: "You returned malformed JSON. Please output only valid JSON that matches the schema: {..} and nothing else. Do not include explanation."

Anna: Regex cleanup as a last resort (dangerous): strip leading non-JSON chars and HTML tags then attempt parse. Example patterns we gave them: 
```
# strip leading garbage before first { or [
raw = raw.replace(/^[^\{\[]+/, '')
# strip simple HTML tags
raw = raw.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '')
```
Note: warn customers this can mask root causes. Use only when you control the client and have retries guarded.

Sara: We also advised immediate mitigation steps for the customer: 1) stop aggressive retries (switch to backoff), 2) rotate token properly and ensure no in-flight requests use the old token, 3) upgrade SDK to latest where we check status before parse. They patched retry backoff and saw errors drop.

Anna: Billing follow-up — because their client retried 100s of times, they were billed for many token attempts. @billing-ops please review for potential refund or credit while we sort root cause.

billing-ops: Assigned case BILL-7891, will review usage spikes and the request_ids provided.

support-bot: Created support ticket SUP-4123 and linked BILL-7891. Eng runtime looped in.

Brian: If we confirm this is due to streaming trailer bug on the server side (HTML injected into stream for 403/401), escalate to eng-runtime with request_id, raw_response (base64), proxy logs, and client sdk version. Collect also the exact time window and customer IP.

Cheng: Escalation note to eng-runtime: likely bug where error path writes HTML to the same stream without closing JSON frame. Repro with expired token + streaming=true.

Anna: Suggested short-term quickfix we pushed: server: on error, set Content-Type: text/plain and terminate stream with status code before any JSON frames are emitted. SDKs: on parse error, validate headers and if status!=200 bail early.

Brian: Final checklist for this thread (what we need from customer): request_ids (done), full raw_response (done), SDK logs with timings, copy of retry policy, consent for billing review. Once we have that eng-runtime will triage.

Sara: Thanks team — customer applied backoff and rotated token; errors dropped ~90%. Leaving ticket open for billing review + eng-runtime triage. :white_check_mark:
